sections.heading: India's energy needs, deficit, resources & dependence

blocks.text: India is the **world's third-largest energy consumer**, with rapidly rising demand. It relies heavily on **coal and imported oil/gas**, faces an **energy deficit and import dependence**, and is pivoting towards **renewables** for security and sustainability.

rows: **Coal dominant (~55% of power)**; oil & gas largely imported; growing renewables.
India imports **~85% of crude oil** and much natural gas.
Coal (large reserves), limited oil/gas, hydro, solar/wind potential, uranium/thorium.
**Conventional** (coal, oil, gas, nuclear, hydro) vs **non-conventional/renewable** (solar, wind, bio).
**Energy security + net-zero by 2070**; 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.

sections.heading: ⚡ Exam-ready deep coverage: India's energy scenario

items: **Energy mix**: coal dominates power (~50%+); India is a big **crude-oil & gas importer (~85% oil import dependence)** → energy-security concern; rising **renewables**.
**Sources**: conventional (coal, oil, gas, hydro, nuclear) vs non-conventional/renewable (solar, wind, biomass, small-hydro, geothermal, tidal).
**Institutions**: Ministries of Power, Coal, Petroleum, New & Renewable Energy (**MNRE**); **NTPC, ONGC, Coal India, NHPC, SECI**.
**Targets**: **500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030**, 50% energy from renewables, **Net-Zero by 2070** (Panchamrit, COP26); energy efficiency (BEE star ratings, PAT scheme, UJALA-LED).

blocks.text: **Solar, wind and nuclear** are the pillars of India's low-carbon energy strategy. Solar and wind are **renewable**; nuclear is a **clean but non-renewable** high-density source, with India pursuing a distinctive **thorium-based three-stage** programme.

rows: Photovoltaic/thermal; India among world leaders; **Bhadla (Rajasthan)** among world's largest solar parks.
India a top-5 wind-power nation; **Tamil Nadu, Gujarat** lead.
**Homi Bhabha's 3-stage programme** — PHWR (uranium) → FBR (plutonium) → **thorium**; India has vast thorium.
**Tarapur, Kudankulam (largest), Kaiga, Kakrapar**; regulated by **AERB**; run by **NPCIL**.

sections.heading: ⚡ Exam-ready deep coverage: solar, wind & nuclear

items: **Solar**: PV (photovoltaic) & thermal; India has huge potential (Rajasthan, Gujarat, AP-Anantapur/Kurnool); intermittency needs storage (batteries).
**Wind**: onshore (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, AP-Rayalaseema) & emerging offshore; India ~4th in wind capacity.

**Nuclear — Homi Bhabha's 3-stage programme**: (1) **PHWR** using natural uranium (produces Pu-239), (2) **Fast Breeder Reactors** using Pu + thorium (**Kalpakkam PFBR**), (3) **thorium-based** reactors (India has ~25% of world thorium — Kerala/AP beach sands, monazite).
**Reactors**: Tarapur (first), Kudankulam (Russia), Kalpakkam; regulator **AERB**; India in NSG waiver (2008 Indo-US nuclear deal) though not NPT signatory.

sections.heading: Environmental issues, legal aspects, policies & treaties

blocks.text: India addresses **environmental issues** through a framework of **constitutional provisions, laws (EPA, Air/Water Acts), institutions (NGT, CPCB) and international treaties** — balancing development with ecological protection.

rows: **Environment (Protection) Act 1986, Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Forest Conservation Act 1980**.
**Stockholm (1972), Rio (1992), Montreal (ozone), Basel, Ramsar (wetlands), CITES, UNFCCC/Paris, CBD**.

sections.heading: 🌿 Exam-ready deep coverage: environmental law, policy & treaties

items: **Indian laws**: **Environment (Protection) Act 1986** (umbrella), **Water Act 1974 & Air Act 1981** (CPCB/SPCB), **Wildlife Protection Act 1972**, **Forest Conservation Act 1980**, **Biological Diversity Act 2002 (NBA)**, **EIA Notification 2006**, **NGT Act 2010**.

**International treaties**: **Stockholm 1972** (first), **Ramsar 1971** (wetlands), **CITES 1973** (trade in species), **Montreal Protocol 1987** (ozone/CFCs), **Basel** (hazardous waste), **CBD 1992 → Nagoya/Cartagena Protocols**, **UNCCD** (desertification), **UNFCCC → Kyoto → Paris**, **Minamata** (mercury), **Stockholm POPs**.
**Institutions**: MoEFCC, CPCB, NGT, NBA, Wildlife Board, Zoological/Botanical Surveys.
**Principles**: polluter pays, precautionary principle, sustainable development, public trust doctrine — upheld by the SC/NGT.

blocks.text: **Biodiversity** is the variety of life — genes, species and ecosystems. India is a **megadiverse country** with rich biological wealth, but faces serious threats from **habitat loss, poaching, invasive species and climate change**, prompting conservation laws and initiatives.

rows: One of **17 megadiverse countries**; **4 biodiversity hotspots** (Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland/Nicobar).
Ecosystem services, food, medicine, climate regulation, livelihoods.
**Habitat loss, poaching, pollution, invasive species, climate change**.
**In-situ (parks, reserves), ex-situ (zoos, gene banks); Biological Diversity Act 2002; NBA**.

items: **Biodiversity levels**: genetic, species, ecosystem; India = a **mega-diverse** country (~8% of world species) with **4 biodiversity hotspots** — **Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar)**.

**Conservation**: **in-situ** (biosphere reserves-18, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, tiger/elephant reserves, community reserves, sacred groves) vs **ex-situ** (zoos, botanical gardens, gene/seed banks, cryopreservation).
**IUCN Red List** categories: Extinct → Critically Endangered → Endangered → Vulnerable → Near Threatened → Least Concern.
**Threats**: habitat loss, poaching, invasive species, pollution, climate change; **Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant, CAMPA**; **CBD/Nagoya** access & benefit-sharing.
**AP biodiversity**: Eastern Ghats endemics (red sanders — Seshachalam), Coringa mangroves, Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam tiger reserve.
